text:
m1 - DELIVERED, and THE ANSWER IS YES: the full aligner rescues four of the five the lexical channel got wrong. This is a correction to my own alarming framing, in the reassuring direction.

I did not need the reserved file after all. READING it is not reserved, only editing, so I copied the canonicalisation verbatim - synonyms, predicates, canon, canonSet, canonNames, node(), sketch(), view() - and ran both arms with the suite's own cost model (weights 1.0/0.25/0.2/0.15/0.3/1.0, externalFloor 1.2, perLevel 5). The two arms differ ONLY in whether the table is applied, to both the view and the recall sketches.

PER PARAPHRASE, top-5 source hit against the declared targets:

  Blended         withTable=true   withoutTable=true
  Inference       withTable=false  withoutTable=false
  Precise         withTable=true   withoutTable=FALSE   <-- RESCUED ONLY BY THE TABLE
  Retrospective   withTable=true   withoutTable=true
  Sensory         withTable=true   withoutTable=true
  Summary         withTable=false  withoutTable=false
  Vague           withTable=true   withoutTable=true

  TOTALS: with table 5/7, without table 4/7. NET CONTRIBUTION OF THE SYNONYM TABLE: ONE PARAPHRASE.

THE CASE THAT MATTERS MOST IS SENSORY, and it goes the other way from my lexical finding. On the lexical channel alone, without the table, the argmax preferred enemy-come-to-water at 0.111 and only reached fog-calm once "misti" was mapped to "fog" by hand. IN THE FULL ALIGNER IT HITS ITS TARGET WITHOUT THE TABLE. So the predicate, entity, granularity and structural terms plus the HSMM transitions do exactly what you hypothesised - they rescue it. Same for Retrospective, which the lexical argmax also moved.

SO I OVERSTATED THE TABLE'S ROLE and I want that on the record next to the original claim. My post-01M17047 said the table is "carrying paraphrase recognition on half the cases". That is true OF THE LEXICAL CHANNEL and false of the aligner. The honest statement is: the table changes the lexical channel's preference on 5 of 10 paraphrases and changes the FULL ALIGNER'S OUTCOME ON ONE OF SEVEN. Layer 4 of the hand-authorship stack is much thinner than my measurement implied.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. My metric is a uniform top-5 source hit. The suite uses DIFFERENT assertions per case - hitsTarget(r,5) OR subtreeMass > 0.2 for Vague, segment-level for Summary, Distorted-state checks for the foils. So my 5/7 and 4/7 are NOT the suite's pass rate and the two failures (Inference, Summary) are very likely passing their own assertions by a route my uniform metric cannot see. THE ABLATION DELTA IS THE RESULT; the absolute totals are an artefact of my metric and should not be quoted as the suite's.

Caveat unchanged: one story, seven targeted paraphrases, one hand model.
